title: Where do idli-vada numbers sit for different pairs?
description: The idli-vada game is played up to sixty with three pairs of numbers, and two overlapping circles hold the multiples of each number. The overlap shows the numbers in both lists, and Keeko's doubt, that the first one is found by multiplying the two numbers, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: the overlap of two circles holds the common multiples, and the first one is found by writing both lists, not by multiplying. Watch for students who multiply the two numbers and call the answer the first common multiple.

source: Play the idli-vada game with different pairs of numbers
video_script.why: The child sees the common multiples of three pairs of numbers sit in the overlap of two circles, and that they are the multiples of one number for each pair.
video_script.substitution: Write the multiples of each number up to sixty, and the numbers in both lists go in the overlap.
video_script.anchor: the idli-vada game played up to sixty with three pairs of numbers, drawn as two overlapping circles
video_script.wrong_answer: the first common multiple of four and six is twenty four
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the first common multiple of four and six is twenty four, after multiplying four by six. Twelve is in both lists and comes first, so the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The common multiples are the multiples of ten, twenty one and twelve

final_answer.spoken: the multiples of ten, twenty one and twelve

hold_back: multiples of ten, twenty one and twelve
never_show: the overlap numbers as multiples of 10, 21 and 12 before the answer
maths_rules: 2 and 5 up to 60: multiples of 5 are 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55, 60; those also multiples of 2 are 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60
3 and 7 up to 60: multiples of 7 are 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, 56; those also multiples of 3 are 21 and 42 (21 = 3 x 7, 42 = 3 x 14)
4 and 6 up to 60: multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 54, 60; those also multiples of 4 are 12, 24, 36, 48, 60
the overlaps are the multiples of 10, 21 and 12 respectively
slip: 4 x 6 = 24 is a common multiple of 4 and 6, but 12 is in both lists and comes first
video_script.design: One idea: the overlap of two circles holds the numbers that are multiples of both. Assumes common multiples are known. Wrong idea: multiply the two numbers to get the first common multiple. The circles stay on the board to the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the idli-vada game with different pairs of numbers.
<bookmark mark='pairs'/>The pairs are two and five, three and seven, and four and six.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Idli is for multiples of the smaller number, and vada for multiples of the larger. Idli-vada is for common multiples.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The game is played up to sixty. Where do the idli-vada numbers sit in the circles for each pair?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: two overlapping circles; the left circle is labelled multiples of the smaller number, the right circle multiples of the larger number, the overlap is shaded

marks.left: the left circle is labelled with the smaller number and the right circle with the larger number

beats.colours: left circle teal, right circle orange, overlap green
narration: <bookmark mark='circles'/>Draw two circles that overlap, like the picture in your book.
<bookmark mark='left'/>The left circle holds multiples of the smaller number. The right circle holds multiples of the larger number.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>The overlap holds the numbers that are multiples of both.

beats.on_screen: Given: the pairs 2 and 5, 3 and 7, 4 and 6; the game is played up to 60

marks.given: the three pairs and the limit are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the pairs two and five, three and seven, and four and six, played up to sixty.

beats.on_screen: To find: the numbers in the overlap for each pair

marks.find: the words To find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the numbers in the overlap for each pair.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 2 and 5. Multiples of 5 up to 60: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55, 60. Also multiples of 2: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, placed in the overlap

marks.fives: the multiples of 5 up to 60 are written
marks.both: the multiples of 5 that are also multiples of 2 move into the overlap

narration: <bookmark mark='fives'/>Step one, take two and five. Write the multiples of five up to sixty.
<bookmark mark='both'/>Keep those that are also multiples of two, because the overlap needs both. They are ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty and sixty.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 3 and 7. Multiples of 7 up to 60: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, 56. Also multiples of 3: 21 and 42, placed in the overlap

marks.sevens: the multiples of 7 up to 60 are written
marks.list: the eight numbers glow one by one

narration: <bookmark mark='sevens'/>Step two, take three and seven. Write the multiples of seven up to sixty.
<bookmark mark='list'/>They are seven, fourteen, twenty one, twenty eight, thirty five, forty two, forty nine and fifty six.
<bookmark mark='both'/>Only twenty one and forty two are also multiples of three, because three goes into them exactly.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 4 and 6. Multiples of 6 up to 60: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 54, 60. Also multiples of 4: 12, 24, 36, 48, 60, placed in the overlap

marks.sixes: the multiples of 6 up to 60 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='sixes'/>Step three, take four and six. Write the multiples of six up to sixty: six, twelve, eighteen, twenty four, thirty, and on.
<bookmark mark='both'/>Keep those that are also multiples of four. They are twelve, twenty four, thirty six, forty eight and sixty.

beats.on_screen: Answer: the common multiples are the multiples of 10, 21 and 12

marks.match: 10, 21 and 12 are joined to the pairs 2 and 5, 3 and 7, 4 and 6

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The common multiples are the multiples of ten, twenty one and twelve.
<bookmark mark='match'/>Ten is for two and five, twenty one for three and seven, twelve for four and six.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the three circle pictures
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt in a bubble, then struck through; the list of 4s and the list of 6s are written and 12 sits in both before 24

marks.twelve: the lists of 4s and 6s are written and 12 lights up in both

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the first common multiple of four and six is twenty four, after multiplying four by six.
<bookmark mark='twelve'/>But twelve is in the list of fours and in the list of sixes too.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Twelve comes before twenty four, so twenty four cannot be the first one.
